beardNotes: Oval faces suit almost any beard style. A short boxed beard or light stubble adds definition; avoid a long pointed beard, which over-elongates the face. Keep the neckline clean and above the Adam's apple.
description: The balanced face shape: forehead slightly wider than the chin, cheekbones are the widest point, and the jawline is softly rounded with a gentle chin. Facial length is about 1.5 times the width.
glassesNotes: Most frame shapes work. Slightly wider-than-tall frames (rectangular, wayfarer, round) look great. Avoid frames narrower than your cheekbones, which can look pinched.

haircuts.description: A timeless cut with 3-5 inches on top, neatly tapered sides, parted to one side.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; style with a light matte product in the morning.
haircuts.name: Classic Side Part
haircuts.whyItWorks: Oval faces are naturally balanced, so the goal is to preserve proportion. The side part adds polish without adding height or width that would distort the balance.

haircuts.description: Short sides with a textured, forward-styled top around 2-3 inches long.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3 weeks; low daily effort with a sea-salt or texture spray.
haircuts.name: Textured Crop
haircuts.whyItWorks: The textured top adds interest without exaggeration; short sides keep the face from looking wider, preserving oval proportions.

haircuts.description: Medium-to-long top swept upward and back, with shorter faded or tapered sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 2-3 weeks; requires daily blow-drying and a medium-hold product.
haircuts.name: Pompadour
haircuts.whyItWorks: The upward volume draws the eye vertically, emphasizing the natural oval length and making the face look strong rather than wide.

haircuts.description: A uniform short cut, typically a #2 to #4 guard all over.
haircuts.maintenance: Self-maintainable; re-trim every 2-3 weeks.
haircuts.name: Buzz Cut (Clean)
haircuts.whyItWorks: Shows off balanced bone structure cleanly. Works best when the head shape underneath is even, with no bumps or asymmetry.

name: Oval
traits: Forehead slightly wider than chin
Cheekbones are the widest point of the face
Rounded jawline with a soft, gentle chin
Face length roughly 1.5x the width

beardNotes: Beards are the round face's best tool — they add length and angles. Keep sides short and the bottom longer and shaped to a rounded or square point at the chin. Avoid full bushy cheeks, which widen the face.
description: The youthful face shape: width and length are nearly equal, the forehead and jawline are softly rounded, and the cheeks are the fullest part.
glassesNotes: Angular frames work best: rectangular, square, and wayfarer styles add structure. Avoid round frames, which echo and amplify the face's roundness.

haircuts.description: Faded or tightly tapered sides with 3-6 inches of textured volume on top, styled upward.
haircuts.maintenance: Fade every 2-3 weeks; daily blow-dry upward with a matte clay for hold.
haircuts.name: High Fade with Height on Top
haircuts.whyItWorks: Height on top adds vertical length to the face while tight sides remove width at the cheeks — the single most flattering combination for round faces.

haircuts.description: Longer, voluminous top (4+ inches) with shaved or very short disconnected sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Sides every 2 weeks; top every 6-8 weeks; daily styling needed.
haircuts.name: Undercut
haircuts.whyItWorks: The contrast between the tight sides and long top slims the cheeks and adds the illusion of length. Swept back or to the side for best effect.

haircuts.description: Top pushed up and slightly back with texture, sides medium-tapered.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; needs a blow-dryer and matte product daily.
haircuts.name: Textured Quiff
haircuts.whyItWorks: Forward and upward motion lifts the face visually; texture on top draws the eye up and away from cheek fullness.

haircuts.description: Asymmetric fringe cut at an angle across the forehead, sides tapered.
haircuts.maintenance: Fringe trim every 2-3 weeks; low daily effort.
haircuts.name: Angular Fringe
haircuts.whyItWorks: The diagonal line breaks up the roundness of the face, introducing angles where there are none naturally.

name: Round
traits: Face width and length are close to equal
Forehead and jawline are rounded, not angular
Cheeks are the widest and fullest part
Soft, low chin with minimal jaw definition

beardNotes: Keep the beard short on the sides and slightly fuller at the chin to elongate the lower face. A rounded beard shape softens the squared jaw; avoid sharp, squared-off cheek lines that double down on the angles.
description: The strong face shape: the forehead, cheekbones, and jawline are all similar in width, with a sharp, defined jaw and a flat-ish chin.
glassesNotes: Round and oval frames soften angular features beautifully. Avoid square or sharp rectangular frames, which over-emphasize the squareness.

haircuts.description: Short-to-medium top (2-3 inches) with texture and a side sweep, tapered sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; quick morning styling.
haircuts.name: Textured Ivy League
haircuts.whyItWorks: Softer texture on top contrasts with the angular jaw, balancing strength with approachability. Side sweep avoids emphasizing the squared hairline.

haircuts.description: Short crew length on top swept to the side, high taper on the sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3 weeks; very low daily effort.
haircuts.name: Side-Swept Crew
haircuts.whyItWorks: The diagonal sweep softens the squared forehead and hairline, while the short length keeps everything clean and proportionate.

haircuts.description: Medium-length top (5+ inches) slicked back, sides faded or tapered.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 4-6 weeks; daily styling with a medium-hold product.
haircuts.name: Long Slick Back
haircuts.whyItWorks: Volume slicked backward adds length above the strong jaw, drawing the face upward and giving a polished, commanding presence.

haircuts.description: Rounded, voluminous top with softly blended tapered sides — no harsh lines.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; blow-dry for volume.
haircuts.name: Soft Taper with Volume
haircuts.whyItWorks: Rounded top lines offset the jaw's angles, creating a balanced look that reads confident rather than severe.

name: Square
traits: Forehead, cheekbones, and jaw are near-equal width
Strong, angular, well-defined jawline
Flat or squared chin
Overall structured, masculine bone structure

beardNotes: A beard adds width to the lower face and shortens its appearance — ideal here. Keep it fuller on the sides and shorter at the chin; avoid pointed goatees or long beards that add more length.
description: A long face shape: length is clearly greater than width, with a tall forehead, narrow cheeks, and often a longer chin. Similar to oval but stretched vertically.
glassesNotes: Taller frames with some height (aviators, larger rectangles) help break up face length. Avoid narrow, thin frames that emphasize verticality.

haircuts.description: Hair worn forward over the forehead in a textured fringe, sides kept medium to full.
haircuts.maintenance: Fringe trim every 2-3 weeks; texture spray or clay for styling.
haircuts.name: Fringe or Fringe with Texture
haircuts.whyItWorks: A fringe covers forehead height, visually shortening the face — the single most effective correction for oblong faces.

haircuts.description: Shoulder-to-collar-length layered hair with volume at the sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 6-8 weeks; air-dry or diffuse.
haircuts.name: Medium-Length Layers
haircuts.whyItWorks: Side volume adds width where the oblong face is narrowest, restoring visual balance.

haircuts.description: Classic side part kept controlled and flat on top, with fuller sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; minimal styling.
haircuts.name: Side Part (Low Volume Top)
haircuts.whyItWorks: Keeping the top flat avoids adding more height; fuller sides add width. The opposite approach to round-face styling.

haircuts.description: Natural waves on a medium crop, sides cut at a medium length rather than faded tight.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 4 weeks; enhance waves with salt spray.
haircuts.name: Wavy Crop with Sides Kept
haircuts.whyItWorks: Waves and volume at the sides widen the mid-face, counteracting vertical length.

name: Oblong
traits: Face length clearly exceeds width
Tall forehead and narrow cheeks
Chin may be longer or more prominent
Similar to oval but stretched vertically

beardNotes: A chin-focused beard (goatee, chin strap, or a fuller chin with shorter sides) adds weight to the narrow lower face. This is one of the few face shapes where a goatee genuinely works well.
description: The tapered face shape: a wide forehead and prominent cheekbones that narrow down to a smaller, often pointed chin.
glassesNotes: Bottom-heavy or rimless frames balance a wide forehead. Round and oval frames work well; avoid top-heavy or oversized frames that widen the forehead further.

haircuts.description: Hair 4-6 inches long with volume around the ears and jawline, softly layered.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 6-8 weeks; blow-dry with volume at the sides.
haircuts.name: Medium Length with Side Volume
haircuts.whyItWorks: Volume at the jawline balances the wide forehead, filling out the narrow lower face so proportions feel even.

haircuts.description: A sweeping fringe covering part of the forehead, medium-length sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Fringe trim every 3 weeks; easy daily styling.
haircuts.name: Side-Swept Fringe
haircuts.whyItWorks: The fringe reduces the visual width of the forehead while keeping the lower face open and balanced.

haircuts.description: Layered, tousled hair with pieces falling around the ears and jaw.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 6-8 weeks; texture product for definition.
haircuts.name: Textured Mid-Length Shag
haircuts.whyItWorks: Layers around the jaw add perceived width exactly where the heart face needs it; the tousled texture keeps it youthful.

haircuts.description: Faded sides starting low, with 3-5 inches of textured top swept loosely to the side.
haircuts.maintenance: Fade every 2-3 weeks; daily styling needed.
haircuts.name: Low Fade with Longer Top
haircuts.whyItWorks: The low fade keeps volume lower on the sides, which balances the narrow chin; the swept top avoids widening the forehead.

name: Heart
traits: Wide forehead, often with a widow's peak
High, prominent cheekbones
Narrow jawline and smaller or pointed chin
Face narrows distinctly from top to bottom

beardNotes: A full beard adds width to the narrow chin and jaw, balancing the cheekbones. Keep it fuller at the jawline; a chin-heavy beard also works to give the lower face more presence.
description: The angular face shape: narrow forehead and jawline with very wide, high cheekbones as the dominant feature.
glassesNotes: Cat-eye, oval, and rimless styles complement the cheekbone line. Avoid narrow frames that make the cheekbones look wider by comparison.

haircuts.description: Textured fringe across the forehead with volume on top, medium-length sides.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; texture spray for the fringe.
haircuts.name: Fringe with Volume on Top
haircuts.whyItWorks: The fringe widens the narrow forehead visually, while top volume balances the dominant cheekbones.

haircuts.description: Hair swept across with natural volume, falling slightly over the ears.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 5-6 weeks; low-effort styling.
haircuts.name: Side-Swept Mid-Length
haircuts.whyItWorks: Hair covering the cheekbone edges softens the widest point of the face and adds width at the forehead line.

haircuts.description: Shorter textured top with tousled movement, sides kept medium.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 3-4 weeks; matte product for texture.
haircuts.name: Textured Crop with Tousled Top
haircuts.whyItWorks: Tousled volume at the top draws attention upward to the forehead line, counterbalancing the cheekbones.

haircuts.description: Longer hair with face-framing layers around the cheekbones and jaw.
haircuts.maintenance: Trim every 8 weeks; conditioner-focused care for length.
haircuts.name: Shoulder-Length Layers
haircuts.whyItWorks: Longer hair softens and frames the wide cheekbones, adding fullness at the forehead and jaw levels for overall balance.

name: Diamond
traits: Narrow forehead and narrow chin
Very wide, prominent, high cheekbones
Cheekbones are the dominant facial feature
Angular overall with a defined bone structure
